+# Did a session read a LATER copy of a file the PR touched? Answer-bearing paths: the paths under .claude/
+# named by the PR fixture's head.diff headers (`diff --git a/X b/Y` both names, quoted C-style names
+# unquoted, `--- a/X`, `+++ b/Y`, `rename from|to X`; /dev/null and unsafe paths dropped) or present under
+# its head/ or base/ tree. Over transcripts/events-{BARE,REVIEW,AUDIT}.jsonl each assistant tool_use is
+# correlated with its tool_result by id. Paths are resolved against the session's cwd (the system init
+# event's, default /workspace, which is also the workspace root), `cd DIR` segments, NAME=value
+# assignments (H=pr/head) and `for V in w…; do` lists; a path inside the workspace and outside pr/ is a
+# workspace operand, pr/head/X and pr/base/X are PR operands.
+#   diff form — a Bash segment (split on newline, ; && || | & outside quotes and parentheses; heredoc bodies
+#   removed first) whose executable is diff, sdiff or comm, or git with diff and --no-index, without -q
+#   (alone or in a short-flag cluster), --brief or --quiet, holding a PR operand and a workspace operand that
+#   names an answer path (or a directory above one); a head.diff operand is never a PR operand. Its result
+#   is split into per-file sections at `diff `, `--- ` and `*** ` header lines (text no header attributes
+#   goes to every target of the command); unified `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` and normal `NaM,b` / `N,Mc…` / `Nd…`
+#   ranges are read (head side, below); a planted site of that file within ±3 of a range, or its must_match
+#   text (stripped, first 50 characters, at least 12) in the section, marks the defect exposed (how diff);
+#   a non-empty section that is not only error lines and yields neither ranges nor must_match marks every
+#   other defect of that file exposed_unknown. Text no header attributes, in a command with several
+#   targets, exposes a defect only with corroboration: a range near the site AND a line of the fixture's
+#   head/X within ±3 of the site in that text, or must_match. A diff whose output is discarded or reduced
+#   (>/dev/null, | wc, | grep -c|-q|-l, | cmp) and a tool_result flagged is_error print no content.
+#   read form — a Bash segment whose executable is cat, sed, awk, grep, head, tail, less or python3, or a
+#   Read (file_path) / Grep (path) tool_use, naming a workspace answer path (a directory for grep or Grep
+#   covers the answer paths below it), whose result contains a LATER-ONLY line within ±3 of a planted site
+#   (when the tool_use reads several answer paths, on a result line that names the file's basename):
+#   a line of the sandbox copy (sandbox/<X>, read bounded and symlink-refusing) present in neither the
+#   fixture's head/X nor base/X, at least 8 characters stripped, mapped to head coordinates by difflib.
+# Either form is skipped for a path whose sandbox copy byte-equals the fixture's head/X or base/X (a closed
+# mount, in either overlay mode: a diff there prints the PR's own change, not a later one).
+# Ranges are read on the head side only: planted sites are head coordinates, so the side of the pr/head
+# operand (left when it precedes the workspace operand) is tested; a pr/base operand gives both sides.
+# grade.json: oracle_exposed_defects (positions d1 … of defects exposed by diff or read),
+# oracle_exposed_unknown (positions only exposed_unknown), oracle_exposed_events [{phase, event: the
+# tool_use's line number in its events file, how: diff|read|exposed_unknown, path}] and
+# oracle_exposed_by_form {diff: [positions], read: [positions]}; null for build tasks.
+# A LOWER BOUND, like the contamination scan: a paraphrase, a copy made by a program and read later, or a
+# path built at run time is not seen.
+ORACLE_PHASES = ("BARE", "REVIEW", "AUDIT")
+DIFF_EXE = {"diff", "sdiff", "comm"}
+READ_EXE = {"cat", "sed", "awk", "grep", "head", "tail", "less", "python3"}
+ANSWER_TOP = ".claude/"
+SEG_KEYWORDS = {"do", "then", "else", "elif", "if", "while", "until", "{", "(", "!", "time"}
+PATHISH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_./@%+,:=~$-]*[A-Za-z0-9_./@%+:~$-]")
+HUNK_U = re.compile(r"^@@ -(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@", re.M)
+HUNK_N = re.compile(r"^(\d+)(?:,(\d+))?([acd])(\d+)(?:,(\d+))?\s*$", re.M)
+ERR_LINE = re.compile(r"^(?:diff|sdiff|comm|git|cat|grep|sed|head|tail|awk|less):|^(?:fatal|error|warning):|"
+                      r"No such file|Is a directory|hook error|BLOCKED|^\s*$|^\s*(?:rc|exit)\s*=\s*\d+\s*$")
+DIFF_BODY = re.compile(r"^[<>+\- @\\0-9]|^---$")
+FILEISH = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+|[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6}\b")
+# a diff whose stdout is counted, tested or discarded prints no content: | wc, | grep -c/-q/-l, >/dev/null
+SILENT_SINK = re.compile(r"^(?:wc|cmp|true|false|test)\b|^grep\s+(?:-[A-Za-z]*[cql][A-Za-z]*|--count|--quiet|--files-with-matches)\b")
+DEVNULL = re.compile(r"(?:^|[\s;])(?:1?>|&>|>&)\s*/dev/null")
+
+
+def unquote_c(q):
+    """a git C-quoted path body (between the quotes) → text"""
+    i, b = 0, bytearray()
+    while i < len(q):
+        ch = q[i]
+        if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(q):
+            n = q[i + 1]
+            if n in "01234567" and re.match(r"[0-7]{3}", q[i + 1:i + 4]):
+                b.append(int(q[i + 1:i + 4], 8))
+                i += 4
+                continue
+            b.extend({"n": b"\n", "t": b"\t", '"': b'"', "\\": b"\\"}.get(n, n.encode()))
+            i += 2
+            continue
+        b.extend(ch.encode())
+        i += 1
+    return b.decode("utf-8", "replace")
+
+
+def answer_paths(pr):
+    names = set()
+    text = read_regular(os.path.join(pr, "head.diff"), 64 * 1024 * 1024, root=pr) or ""
+    Q = r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"'
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        if line.startswith("diff --git "):
+            rest = line[len("diff --git "):]
+            m = re.fullmatch(Q.replace("((", "a/((", 1) + " " + Q.replace("((", "b/((", 1), rest) or None
+            if m:
+                names.update(unquote_c(x) for x in m.groups())
+                continue
+            m = re.fullmatch(r"a/(\S+) b/(\S+)", rest)
+            if m:
+                names.update(m.groups())
+                continue
+            half = (len(rest) - 1) // 2   # unquoted names with spaces: "a/X b/X" with X twice
+            if rest[:2] == "a/" and rest[half + 1:half + 3] == "b/" and rest[2:half] == rest[half + 3:]:
+                names.add(rest[2:half])
+        elif line.startswith(("--- ", "+++ ")):
+            body = line[4:].split("\t", 1)[0]
+            if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"'):
+                body = unquote_c(body[1:-1])
+            if body.startswith(("a/", "b/")):
+                names.add(body[2:])
+        elif line.startswith(("rename from ", "rename to ", "copy from ", "copy to ")):
+            body = line.split(" ", 2)[2]
+            names.add(unquote_c(body[1:-1]) if body.startswith('"') and body.endswith('"') else body)
+    for side in ("head", "base"):
+        root = os.path.join(pr, side)
+        for r, ds, fs in os.walk(root):
+            for n in fs:
+                names.add(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(r, n), root).replace(os.sep, "/"))
+    out = set()
+    for n in names:
+        parts = safe_rel(n)
+        if parts and n != "/dev/null":
+            rel = "/".join(parts)
+            if rel.startswith(ANSWER_TOP):
+                out.add(rel)
+    return out
+
+
+def split_segments(cmd):
+    """[(segment, separator after it)]: split on newline ; & | (&& || included) outside quotes and
+    parentheses; the separator is "|" for a pipe into the next segment, else ";" """
+    segs, cur, q, depth, i = [], [], None, 0, 0
+    while i < len(cmd):
+        ch = cmd[i]
+        if q == "'":
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "'":
+                q = None
+        elif q == '"':
+            cur.append(ch)
+            if ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+                cur.append(cmd[i + 1])
+                i += 1
+            elif ch == '"':
+                q = None
+        elif ch == "\\" and i + 1 < len(cmd):
+            cur.append(ch + cmd[i + 1])
+            i += 1
+        elif ch in "'\"":
+            q = ch
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == "(":
+            depth += 1
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif ch == ")":
+            depth = max(0, depth - 1)
+            cur.append(ch)
+        elif depth == 0 and ch in "\n;&|":
+            pipe = ch == "|" and cmd[i + 1:i + 2] != "|" and cmd[i - 1:i] != "|"
+            segs.append(("".join(cur), "|" if pipe else ";"))
+            cur = []
+        else:
+            cur.append(ch)
+        i += 1
+    segs.append(("".join(cur), ";"))
+    return [(x.strip(), sep) for x, sep in segs if x.strip()]
+
+
+def seg_words(seg):
+    try:
+        w = shlex.split(seg, comments=False, posix=True)
+    except ValueError:
+        w = seg.split()
+    while w and (w[0] in SEG_KEYWORDS):
+        w = w[1:]
+    while w and re.match(r"^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=", w[0]) and len(w) > 1:
+        w = w[1:]
+    while w and w[0] in ("command", "env", "builtin", "exec", "nice"):
+        w = w[1:]
+    if w and w[0] == "timeout":
+        w = w[1:]
+        while w and (w[0].startswith("-") or re.match(r"^\d+[smhd]?$", w[0])):
+            w = w[1:]
+    return w
+
+
+def expand(tok, vars_):
+    """$NAME / ${NAME} expansion → list of strings (a loop variable expands to every word); an unknown
+    variable leaves the token unresolved (dropped)"""
+    outs = [tok]
+    for _ in range(4):
+        nxt, changed = [], False
+        for o in outs:
+            m = re.search(r"\$\{([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\}|\$([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)", o)
+            if not m:
+                nxt.append(o)
+                continue
+            name = m.group(1) or m.group(2)
+            if name not in vars_:
+                continue
+            changed = True
+            for v in vars_[name]:
+                nxt.append(o[:m.start()] + v + o[m.end():])
+        outs = nxt
+        if not changed:
+            break
+    return [o for o in outs if "$" not in o]
+
+
+def classify(tok, cwd, ws):
+    """→ ("pr", side, rel) | ("ws", rel) | None"""
+    tok = tok.strip("'\"")
+    if not tok or tok.startswith("-") or "://" in tok:
+        return None
+    if tok.startswith("~") or "*" in tok or "?" in tok:
+        return None
+    full = os.path.normpath(tok if tok.startswith("/") else os.path.join(cwd, tok))
+    if full != ws and not full.startswith(ws.rstrip("/") + "/"):
+        return None
+    rel = "" if full == ws else full[len(ws.rstrip("/")) + 1:]
+    if rel == "pr" or rel.startswith("pr/"):
+        rest = rel[3:]
+        for side in ("head", "base"):
+            if rest == side or rest.startswith(side + "/"):
+                return ("pr", side, rest[len(side) + 1:])
+        return ("pr", None, rest)
+    return ("ws", rel)
+
+
+def ws_targets(rel, answer, directory_ok):
+    if rel in answer:
+        return [rel]
+    if not directory_ok:
+        return []
+    pre = "" if rel in ("", ".") else rel.rstrip("/") + "/"
+    return sorted(a for a in answer if a.startswith(pre))
+
+
+def segment_tokens(seg, vars_, cwd, ws):
+    """every path-shaped token of a segment (inside process substitutions too), expanded and classified"""
+    out = []
+    for m in PATHISH.finditer(seg):
+        for v in expand(m.group(0), vars_):
+            c = classify(v, cwd, ws)
+            if c is not None:
+                out.append((v, c))
+    return out
+
+
+def result_text(blk):
+    c = blk.get("content")
+    if isinstance(c, str):
+        return c
+    if isinstance(c, list):
+        return "\n".join(x.get("text", "") for x in c if isinstance(x, dict) and isinstance(x.get("text"), str))
+    return ""
+
+
+def ranges_of(text, sides=("left", "right")):
+    """the printed line ranges of a unified or normal diff on the given sides (left = first operand)"""
+    rs = []
+    for m in HUNK_U.finditer(text):
+        a, n = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2) or 1)
+        c, k = int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4) or 1)
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, a + max(n, 1) - 1))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, c + max(k, 1) - 1))
+    for m in HUNK_N.finditer(text):
+        a = int(m.group(1))
+        c = int(m.group(4))
+        if "left" in sides:
+            rs.append((a, int(m.group(2) or a)))
+        if "right" in sides:
+            rs.append((c, int(m.group(5) or c)))
+    return rs
+
+
+def sections(text, targets):
+    """{target: [section body]}: the result split at header lines — a diff header (diff, ---, +++, ***) or
+    a line that is not diff body and names a file (an `echo "=== $f"` marker); a header naming a target
+    (the longest one it holds) opens that target's section, any other header a dropped one; text before
+    the first header belongs to the sole target. Text no header attributes (several targets) is returned
+    as the loose list. Header lines are not part of a body. → (sections, loose)"""
+    out = {f: [] for f in targets}
+    loose = []
+    cur = targets[0] if len(targets) == 1 else None
+    buf = []
+
+    def flush():
+        if buf:
+            (out[cur] if cur is not None else loose).append("\n".join(buf))
+
+    for line in text.split("\n"):
+        diff_hdr = line.startswith(("diff ", "--- ", "*** ", "+++ "))
+        if diff_hdr or (not DIFF_BODY.match(line) and FILEISH.search(line)):
+            named = sorted((f for f in targets if f in line), key=len, reverse=True)
+            hit = named[0] if named else None
+            if line.startswith("+++ ") and hit == cur:
+                continue
+            if hit is not None or diff_hdr or len(targets) > 1:
+                flush()
+                buf = []
+                cur = hit
+                continue
+        buf.append(line)
+    flush()
+    return out, loose
+
+
+def oracle_scan(t, run_dir):
+    try:
+        pr = resolve_pr_fixture(t)
+    except GradeError:
+        return [], [], [], {"diff": [], "read": []}
+    answer = answer_paths(pr)
+    defects = t.key.get("defects") or []
+    by_file = {}
+    for i, d in enumerate(defects, 1):
+        f = d.get("file")
+        if isinstance(f, str) and f in answer:
+            sites = [s for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d.get("anchor_line")]) if isinstance(s, int) and not isinstance(s, bool)]
+            mm = (d.get("must_match") or "").strip()[:50] if isinstance(d.get("must_match"), str) else ""
+            by_file.setdefault(f, []).append((f"d{i}", sites, mm if len(mm) >= 12 else ""))
+    if not by_file:
+        return [], [], [], {"diff": [], "read": []}
+    sb = os.path.join(run_dir, "sandbox")
+    later, live, near_text = {}, {}, {}
+    for f in by_file:
+        cur = read_regular(os.path.join(sb, *f.split("/")), FILE_CAP, root=sb)
+        hd = read_regular(os.path.join(pr, "head", *f.split("/")), FILE_CAP, root=pr)
+        bs = read_regular(os.path.join(pr, "base", *f.split("/")), FILE_CAP, root=pr)
+        live[f] = cur is not None and cur != hd and cur != bs
+        later[f] = []
+        if not live[f] or hd is None:
+            continue
+        hl, cl = hd.split("\n"), cur.split("\n")
+        for pos, sites, _mm in by_file[f]:
+            near_text[(f, pos)] = [hl[L - 1].strip() for s_ in sites for L in range(s_ - 3, s_ + 4)
+                                   if 1 <= L <= len(hl) and len(hl[L - 1].strip()) >= 8]
+        known = set(x.strip() for x in hl) | (set(x.strip() for x in bs.split("\n")) if bs is not None else set())
+        for tag, i1, i2, j1, j2 in difflib.SequenceMatcher(None, hl, cl, autojunk=False).get_opcodes():
+            if tag == "equal":
+                continue
+            lo, hi = i1 + 1, max(i2, i1 + 1)
+            for j in range(j1, j2):
+                txt = cl[j].strip()
+                if len(txt) >= 8 and txt not in known:
+                    later[f].append((txt, lo, hi))
+    exposed, unknown, events, by_form = {}, {}, [], {"diff": set(), "read": set()}
+
+    def note(phase, ev, how, path, pos):
+        rec = {"phase": phase, "event": ev, "how": how, "path": path}
+        if rec not in events:
+            events.append(rec)
+        (exposed if how != "exposed_unknown" else unknown).setdefault(pos, True)
+        if how in by_form:
+            by_form[how].add(pos)
+
+    def near(sites, lo, hi):
+        return any(not (hi < s - 3 or lo > s + 3) for s in sites)
+
+    for label, path in transcripts(run_dir):
+        if label not in ORACLE_PHASES:
+            continue
+        ws, uses = "/workspace", {}
+        for i, line in enumerate(open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"), 1):
+            try:
+                ev = json.loads(line)
+            except ValueError:
+                continue
+            if not isinstance(ev, dict):
+                continue
+            if ev.get("type") == "system" and isinstance(ev.get("cwd"), str) and ev["cwd"].startswith("/"):
+                ws = os.path.normpath(ev["cwd"])
+                continue
+            content = (ev.get("message") or {}).get("content") if isinstance(ev.get("message"), dict) else None
+            if not isinstance(content, list):
+                continue
+            for blk in content:
+                if not isinstance(blk, dict):
+                    continue
+                if ev.get("type") == "assistant" and blk.get("type") == "tool_use" and isinstance(blk.get("input"), dict):
+                    plan = oracle_plan(blk.get("name") or "", blk["input"], ws, answer)
+                    if plan and isinstance(blk.get("id"), str):
+                        uses[blk["id"]] = (i, plan)
+                elif ev.get("type") == "user" and blk.get("type") == "tool_result" and blk.get("tool_use_id") in uses:
+                    i0, plan = uses.pop(blk["tool_use_id"])
+                    if blk.get("is_error") is True:
+                        continue          # the tool failed (a refused command, a hook block): nothing printed
+                    res = result_text(blk)
+                    dtargets = sorted({f for how, f in plan if how.startswith("diff") and live.get(f)})
+                    rtargets = sorted({f for how, f in plan if how == "read" and live.get(f)})
+                    if dtargets and res.strip():
+                        secs_by, loose = sections(res, dtargets)
+                        # loose text (several targets, no naming header): a range near the site counts only
+                        # with the head file's own text near that site in the same text, or must_match
+                        for sec in loose:
+                            for f in dtargets:
+                                rs = ranges_of(sec, plan_sides(plan, f))
+                                for pos, sites, mm in by_file.get(f, []):
+                                    ranged = any(near(sites, lo, hi) for lo, hi in rs)
+                                    own = any(x in sec for x in near_text.get((f, pos), []))
+                                    if (ranged and own) or (mm and mm in sec):
+                                        note(label, i0, "diff", f, pos)
+                        for f, secs in secs_by.items():
+                            for sec in secs:
+                                body = [l for l in sec.split("\n") if not ERR_LINE.search(l)]
+                                if not body:
+                                    continue
+                                rs = ranges_of(sec, plan_sides(plan, f))
+                                hit_any = False
+                                for pos, sites, mm in by_file.get(f, []):
+                                    if any(near(sites, lo, hi) for lo, hi in rs) or (mm and mm in sec):
+                                        note(label, i0, "diff", f, pos)

+def tree_paths(root):
+    out = set()
+    if not os.path.isdir(root) or os.path.islink(root):
+        return out
+    for d, dirs, files in os.walk(root, followlinks=False):
+        for n in dirs + files:
+            full = os.path.join(d, n)
+            if os.path.islink(full) or os.path.isfile(full):
+                out.add(os.path.relpath(full, root).replace(os.sep, "/"))
+    return out
+
+def fixture_meta(fixture):
+    meta = {}
+    f = os.path.join(fixture, "fixture.yaml")
+    if os.path.isfile(f):
+        for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace"):
+            m = re.match(r'^(head_commit|fix_commit|base_commit):\s*["\']?([0-9a-f]{7,64})["\']?\s*(#.*)?$', line.strip())
+            if m:
+                meta[m.group(1)] = m.group(2)
+    return meta
+
+def in_scope(p):
+    return p is not None and p.startswith(".claude/") and p != ".claude/checksums.json"
+
+def answer_set(fixture, repo):
+    """{path: "pr"|"fix"}, notes, meta"""
+    notes = []
+    if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(fixture, "head.diff")):
+        die("fixture has no head.diff: " + fixture)
+    pr = set()
+    for raw in diff_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "head.diff")) + sorted(tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "head"))) \
+            + sorted(tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, "base"))):
+        if raw is None:
+            continue
+        p = norm(raw)
+        if p is None:
+            notes.append("rejected path %r" % raw)
+            continue
+        pr.add(p)
+    meta = fixture_meta(fixture)
+    fix = set()
+    fc = meta.get("fix_commit")
+    meta["fix_available"] = "none"
+    if fc:
+        out = git(repo, "show", "--no-renames", "--name-only", "-z", "--format=", fc) if has_commit(repo, fc) else None
+        if out is None:
+            notes.append("fix_commit_unavailable " + fc)
+            meta["fix_available"] = "unavailable"
+        else:
+            meta["fix_available"] = "available"
+            for raw in out.decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape").split("\0"):
+                raw = raw.strip("\n")
+                if not raw:
+                    continue
+                p = norm(raw)
+                if p is None:
+                    notes.append("rejected fix path %r" % raw)
+                    continue
+                fix.add(p)
+    hc = meta.get("head_commit")
+    meta["head_available"] = bool(hc) and has_commit(repo, hc)
+    entries = {}
+    for p in sorted(pr | fix):
+        if in_scope(p):
+            entries[p] = "pr" if p in pr else "fix"
+    return entries, notes, meta
+
+def fixture_file(root, path):
+    """(bytes, exec) of a regular file at root/path with no symlink component, else None"""
+    cur = root
+    if os.path.islink(cur) or not os.path.isdir(cur):
+        return None
+    parts = path.split("/")
+    for c in parts:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return None
+    try:
+        st = os.lstat(cur)
+    except OSError:
+        return None
+    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+        return None
+    return open(cur, "rb").read(), bool(st.st_mode & 0o111)
+
+def tree_blob(repo, commit, path):
+    """(bytes, exec, blob_id) of a regular-file entry in commit, else None"""
+    out = git(repo, "ls-tree", "-z", commit, "--", path)
+    if not out:
+        return None
+    ent = out.split(b"\0")[0].decode("utf-8", "surrogateescape")
+    m = re.match(r"^(\d+) (\w+) ([0-9a-f]+)\t(.*)$", ent, re.S)
+    if not m or m.group(2) != "blob" or m.group(4) != path or m.group(1) not in ("100644", "100755"):
+        return None
+    data = git(repo, "cat-file", "blob", m.group(3))
+    if data is None:
+        return None
+    return data, m.group(1) == "100755", m.group(3)
+
+def expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta):
+    """{path: (bytes, exec) | None}"""
+    exp = {}
+    for p, src in entries.items():
+        if src == "pr":
+            exp[p] = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, mode), p)
+        elif meta.get("head_available"):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, meta["head_commit"], p)
+            exp[p] = (tb[0], tb[1]) if tb else None
+        else:
+            exp[p] = None
+    return exp
+
+def state(ws, path):
+    """sha256 of the sandbox file, 'absent', or a non-file marker (never followed)"""
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            return "symlink-component"
+    full = os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+    if os.path.islink(full):
+        return "symlink"
+    if not os.path.lexists(full):
+        return "absent"
+    if not os.path.isfile(full):
+        return "not-a-file"
+    return sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+
+def safe_dst(ws, path):
+    cur = ws
+    for c in path.split("/")[:-1]:
+        cur = os.path.join(cur, c)
+        if os.path.islink(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: symlink component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+        if os.path.lexists(cur) and not os.path.isdir(cur):
+            die("overlay refused: non-directory component %s in the sandbox path of %s" % (os.path.relpath(cur, ws), path))
+    return os.path.join(ws, *path.split("/"))
+
+def remove(dst):
+    if os.path.islink(dst) or (os.path.lexists(dst) and not os.path.isdir(dst)):
+        os.unlink(dst)
+    elif os.path.isdir(dst):
+        shutil.rmtree(dst)
+
+def gate_script(p):
+    return bool(re.match(r"^\.claude/(scripts|hooks)/", p) or re.match(r"^\.claude/skills/[^/]+/SKILL\.md$", p))
+
+def cmd_overlay(ws, fixture, mode, repo):
+    if mode not in ("head", "base"):
+        die("overlay mode must be head or base, got %r" % mode)
+    if not os.path.isdir(ws) or os.path.islink(ws):
+        die("workspace not found: " + ws)
+    entries, notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    for n in notes:
+        note("overlay: " + n)
+    if entries and any(s == "fix" for s in entries.values()) and not meta.get("head_available"):
+        note("overlay: head_commit %s unavailable: fix-commit paths outside the PR are removed" % meta.get("head_commit"))
+    lines, gates, removed = [], [], 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        dst = safe_dst(ws, p)
+        e = exp[p]
+        remove(dst)
+        if e is None:
+            removed += 1
+            note("overlay: removed %s (%s; no %s version)" % (p, entries[p], mode if entries[p] == "pr" else "head_commit"))
+        else:
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst), exist_ok=True)
+            fd = os.open(dst, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0), 0o755 if e[1] else 0o644)
+            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as fh:
+                fh.write(e[0])
+            os.chmod(dst, 0o755 if e[1] else 0o644)
+            if gate_script(p):
+                gates.append(p)
+        lines.append("overlay_sha256=%s=%s" % (p, state(ws, p)))
+    print("mount_overlay=%s:%d" % (mode, len(entries)))
+    for l in lines:
+        print(l)
+    print("overlay_removed=%d" % removed)
+    print("overlay_fix_commit=%s" % meta["fix_available"])
+    print("gate_scripts_at_pr_version=" + ",".join(gates))
+
+def read_evidence(f):
+    ev = {"overlay_sha256": {}}
+    for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape"):
+        line = line.rstrip("\n")
+        if "=" not in line:
+            continue
+        k, v = line.split("=", 1)
+        if k == "overlay_sha256":
+            if "=" in v:
+                p, s = v.rsplit("=", 1)
+                ev["overlay_sha256"].setdefault(p, s)
+        elif k not in ev:
+            ev[k] = v
+    return ev
+
+def cmd_check(ws, fixture, evfile, repo, source_commit):
+    if not os.path.isfile(evfile):
+        print("FAIL (a) -: no arm evidence file"); sys.exit(1)
+    ev = read_evidence(evfile)
+    mo = ev.get("mount_overlay", "")
+    m = re.match(r"^(head|base):(\d+)$", mo)
+    if not m:
+        print("FAIL (a) -: mount_overlay=%s (want head|base:<n>)" % (mo or "<missing>")); sys.exit(1)
+    mode, n = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
+    entries, _notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    fails = []
+    if n != len(entries):
+        fails.append(("a", "-", "mount_overlay names %d paths, the fixture's answer set has %d" % (n, len(entries))))
+    rec = ev["overlay_sha256"]
+    present = 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        want = sha(exp[p][0]) if exp[p] is not None else "absent"
+        got = state(ws, p)
+        if got != "absent":
+            present += 1
+        if p not in rec:
+            fails.append(("c", p, "no overlay_sha256 line"))
+            if got != want:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+            continue
+        if got != rec[p]:
+            if rec[p] == want:
+                fails.append(("c", p, "mount_mutated=%s (pre-run %s, now %s)" % (p, rec[p][:12], got[:12])))
+            else:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "pre-run %s, now %s, want %s (%s)" % (rec[p][:12], got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+        elif got != want:
+            fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+    # (b) later-only pinned versions
+    if not has_commit(repo, source_commit):
+        fails.append(("b", "-", "source commit %s not in %s" % (source_commit or "<none>", repo)))
+        later = {}
+    else:
+        known = set(sha(e[0]) for e in exp.values() if e is not None)
+        for t in ("head", "base"):
+            for q in tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, t)):
+                ff = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, t), q)
+                if ff is not None:
+                    known.add(sha(ff[0]))
+        later = {}
+        for p in sorted(entries):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, source_commit, p)
+            if tb is None or len(tb[0]) == 0:
+                continue
+            h = sha(tb[0])
+            if h in known:
+                continue
+            later.setdefault(h, (p, len(tb[0]), tb[2]))
+        sizes = set(v[1] for v in later.values())
+        scanned = 0
+        if later:
+            for d, dirs, files in os.walk(ws, followlinks=False):
+                rel = os.path.relpath(d, ws)
+                if rel == ".":
+                    dirs[:] = [x for x in dirs if x not in ("pr", ".git")]
+                for nme in sorted(files):
+                    full = os.path.join(d, nme)
+                    try:
+                        st = os.lstat(full)
+                    except OSError:
+                        continue
+                    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+                        continue
+                    scanned += 1
+                    if st.st_size not in sizes:
+                        continue
+                    h = sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+                    if h in later:
+                        fails.append(("b", os.path.relpath(full, ws), "byte-equal to the pinned %s at %s" % (later[h][0], source_commit[:12])))
+    # (d) the sandbox repository
+    base = ev.get("base_commit", "")
+    gd = os.path.join(ws, ".git")
+    if not os.path.isdir(gd) or os.path.islink(gd):
+        fails.append(("d", ".git", "the sandbox has no .git directory"))
+    else:
+        revs = git(ws, "rev-list", "--all")
+        revs = sorted(set(revs.decode().split())) if revs is not None else None
+        if revs != [base]:
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "commits %s, want exactly the base commit %s" % (",".join(r[:12] for r in (revs or [])) or "<unreadable>", base[:12] or "<none>")))
+        rem = git(ws, "remote")
+        if rem is None or rem.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "remote(s): %s" % ((rem or b"<unreadable>").decode(errors="replace").split() or "")))
+        if os.path.lexists(os.path.join(gd, "objects", "info", "alternates")):
+            fails.append(("d", ".git/objects/info/alternates", "the sandbox object store borrows another repository's objects"))
+        unr = git(ws, "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs", "--no-progress")
+        if unr is None or unr.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "fsck --unreachable: %s" % ((unr or b"<failed>").decode(errors="replace").strip().split("\n")[0])))
+        for h, (p, _sz, blob) in sorted(later.items()):
+            if git(ws, "cat-file", "-e", blob) is not None:
+                fails.append(("d", p, "the pinned blob %s of %s is in the sandbox object store" % (blob[:12], p)))
+    if fails:
+        fails.sort(key=lambda f: f[0])
+        c, p, d = fails[0]
+        print("FAIL (%s) %s: %s%s" % (c, p, d, " (+%d more)" % (len(fails) - 1) if len(fails) > 1 else ""))
+        sys.exit(1)
+    print("ok %s:%d answer paths (%d present), %d later-only pinned versions, sandbox git = base commit only"
+          % (mode, len(entries), present, len(later)))
+
+cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else ""
+if cmd == "answer-set" and len(sys.argv) == 4:

+elif cmd == "overlay" and len(sys.argv) == 6:

+elif cmd == "check" and len(sys.argv) == 7:

+    die("usage: overlay <ws> <fixture> <mode> <repo> | check <ws> <fixture> <evidence> <repo> <commit>")

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi

+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"

+  return 0

+# apply_eval_config_variant <ws> — the cycle-131 evaluation config (FR-4, DEC-0618): both
+# gates' budget scales with the diff up to USD 6.00. Evidence config_variant=eval.
+apply_eval_config_variant() {
+  local ws="$1" cfg="$1/.loa.config.yaml" g
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
+  for g in code_review security_audit; do
+    G="$g" yq -i '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale = "diff" | .flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max = 600' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: yq failed on $cfg"; return 2; }
+    [[ "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == diff \
+       && "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == 600 ]] \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done

+  return 0
+}

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# evals/tests/sandbox-mount.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 263 Task 1.1 (PRD FR-1 AC 1, AC 5;
+# FR-5 AC 1; SDD §5.2 overlay_answer_paths / check_mount_closed, D-1.1, D-5.x)
+#
+# evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh's closed mount on a fixture-shaped sandbox: a
+# throwaway source repository (the pinned Loa tree: a head commit, then a fix commit
+# that is the pin), a PR fixture (head.diff, head/, base/, fixture.yaml) whose head.diff
+# carries every path shape (modified, added, deleted, renamed, a quoted path with a
+# space, a symlink in head, a path outside .claude/, a removed hunk line that looks like
+# a header, a binary hunk), and a sandbox built as pipeline-run.sh builds it (pr/ copied,
+# a base commit, the whole .claude/ mounted). Also the cycle-131 toggles (bare_model,
+# dissent, oracle_open) and the eval config variant. No model call, no docker.
+# =============================================================================
+
+setup() {
+  TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+  REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+  LIB="$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh"
+  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/sm.XXXXXX")"
+  SRC="$T/src" FX="$T/fx" W="$T/ws"
+  export ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$T/ev.txt"; : > "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  make_source
+  make_fixture
+  make_ws
+}
+
+teardown() {
+  chmod -R u+rwx "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+  find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
+  rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true
+}
+
+g() { git -C "$1" -c user.email=t@t -c user.name=t -c commit.gpgsign=false "${@:2}"; }
+
+# the pinned Loa tree: commit H (= the PR's head_commit) then commit F (the fix, the pin)
+make_source() {
+  mkdir -p "$SRC/.claude/scripts" "$SRC/.claude/data" "$SRC/.claude/loa" "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1" "$SRC/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'new name head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly head\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf 'skill pinned\n' > "$SRC/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$SRC/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  printf 'outside head\n' > "$SRC/lib/outside.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  chmod +x "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && git init -q && g . add -A && g . commit -qm head )
+  H="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  # the fix commit: later versions of PR paths and of a path the PR never touched
+  printf 'mod LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted LATER restored\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"
+  printf 'new name LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy LATER\n' > "$SRC/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'fixonly LATER fixed\n' > "$SRC/.claude/scripts/fixonly.sh"
+  printf '{"files":{"later":1}}\n' > "$SRC/.claude/checksums.json"
+  ( cd "$SRC" && g . add -A && g . commit -qm fix )
+  F="$(git -C "$SRC" rev-parse HEAD)"
+}
+
+# the PR fixture (immutable in production: evals/fixtures/review-prs/pr-NN/)
+make_fixture() {
+  mkdir -p "$FX/head/.claude/scripts" "$FX/head/.claude/data" "$FX/head/.claude/skills/s1" "$FX/head/lib" \
+           "$FX/base/.claude/scripts" "$FX/base/.claude/data" "$FX/base/lib"
+  printf 'mod head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"; chmod +x "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'mod base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/mod.sh"
+  printf 'added head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/added.sh"
+  printf 'deleted base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh"
+  printf 'old name base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/scripts/old name.sh"
+  printf 'new name head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/scripts/new name.sh"
+  printf 'xy head\n' > "$FX/head/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'xy base\n' > "$FX/base/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+  printf 'SECRET outside the fixture\n' > "$T/outside-secret"
+  ln -s ../../../../outside-secret "$FX/head/.claude/skills/s1/SKILL.md"
+  printf 'outside head\n' > "$FX/head/lib/outside.sh"; printf 'outside base\n' > "$FX/base/lib/outside.sh"
+  cat > "$FX/head.diff" <<'DIFF'
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/mod.sh b/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
+--- a/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
++++ b/.claude/scripts/mod.sh
+@@ -1,2 +1,1 @@

++mod head

+@@ -0,0 +1 @@
++added head
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh b/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh

+--- a/.claude/scripts/deleted.sh
++++ /dev/null
+@@ -1 +0,0 @@
+-deleted base
+diff --git a/.claude/scripts/old name.sh b/.claude/scripts/new name.sh
+similarity 50%
+rename from .claude/scripts/old name.sh
+rename to .claude/scripts/new name.sh
+diff --git "a/.claude/data/x y.txt" "b/.claude/data/x y.txt"
+--- "a/.claude/data/x y.txt"

+@@ -1 +1 @@

++xy head

+diff --git a/lib/outside.sh b/lib/outside.sh

++++ b/lib/outside.sh
+@@ -1 +1 @@
+-outside base
++outside head
+DIFF
+  printf 'name: pr-t\nbase_commit: "%s"\nhead_commit: "%s"\nfix_commit: "%s"\n' "$H" "$H" "$F" > "$FX/fixture.yaml"
+}
+
+# the sandbox as pipeline-run.sh materialises it: pr/, the base commit, then the mount
+make_ws() {
+  mkdir -p "$W/pr"
+  cp -a "$FX/base" "$FX/head" "$FX/head.diff" "$W/pr/"
+  git -C "$W" init -q
+  printf '%s\n' '/.claude/' '/CLAUDE.md' '/.loa.config.yaml' '/grimoires/' '/.run/' '/.beads/' '/.eval/' >> "$W/.git/info/exclude"
+  g "$W" add -A; g "$W" commit -qm base
+  printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$(git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE"
+  mkdir -p "$W/.claude"; cp -a "$SRC/.claude/." "$W/.claude/"

+}

+# lib <fn> <args…> — run one library function in a fresh shell (the library sets no options)
+lib() { run bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source "$1"; shift; "$@"' _ "$LIB" "$@"; }
+ev() { grep -E "^$1=" "$ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE" | sed "s/^$1=//"; }
+content() { cat "$W/$1"; }

+@test "answer set: diff headers (quoted, renamed both names, /dev/null, binary), head/ and base/ files, fix-commit paths; only .claude/, never checksums.json, a removed '--- a/' line or a path outside .claude/" {

+  lib overlay_answer_paths "$W" "$FX" head "$SRC" "$F"

+# make_closed_run — a source repo (head commit H, fix commit F = the pin), a PR fixture and a
+# run dir whose sandbox was materialised and overlaid by the real mount library
+make_closed_run() {
+  local src="$T/c-src" fx="$T/c-fx" rd="$T/c-run" w
+  mkdir -p "$src/.claude/scripts" "$src/.claude/loa"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper head\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  printf 'loa\n' > "$src/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md"
+  ( cd "$src" && git init -q && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm head )
+  CH="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  printf 'gate LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'helper LATER fixed\n' > "$src/.claude/scripts/helper.sh"
+  ( cd "$src" && gg . add -A && gg . commit -qm fix )
+  CF="$(git -C "$src" rev-parse HEAD)"
+  mkdir -p "$fx/head/.claude/scripts" "$fx/base/.claude/scripts"
+  printf 'gate head\n' > "$fx/head/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"; printf 'gate base\n' > "$fx/base/.claude/scripts/gate.sh"
+  printf 'diff --git a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n--- a/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n+++ b/.claude/scripts/gate.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-gate base\n+gate head\n' > "$fx/head.diff"
+  printf 'name: pr-c\nhead_commit: "%s"\nfix_commit: "%s"\n' "$CH" "$CF" > "$fx/fixture.yaml"
+  mkdir -p "$rd/meta" "$rd/sandbox/pr" "$rd/eval"
+  w="$rd/sandbox"
+  cp -a "$fx/head" "$fx/base" "$fx/head.diff" "$w/pr/"
+  git -C "$w" init -q; printf '/.claude/\n' >> "$w/.git/info/exclude"; gg "$w" add -A; gg "$w" commit -qm base
+  printf 'base_commit=%s\n' "$(git -C "$w" rev-parse HEAD)" > "$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt"
+  mkdir -p "$w/.claude"; cp -a "$src/.claude/." "$w/.claude/"
+  ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE="$rd/meta/arm-evidence.txt" bash -c 'source "$1"; overlay_answer_paths "$2" "$3" head "$4" "$5"' _ \
+    "$REPO_ROOT/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh" "$w" "$fx" "$src" "$CF" 2>/dev/null
+  echo a1_closed > "$rd/meta/arm"
+  jq -n --arg sc "$CF" '{schema_version: 1, arm: "a1_closed", task_id: "rc-c", task_type: "review-catch", status: "completed",

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget-scale.bats — cycle-131 Sprint 1 Task 1.8 (PRD FR-4, SDD D-4.2).
+#
+# flatline_protocol.<code_review|security_audit>.budget_scale: fixed | diff (default fixed) and budget_cents_max
+# (default 600). With diff the gate's budget is min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max); an
+# estimate above that still refuses (exit 4, status budget_exceeded, reason budget). A malformed scale or maximum
+# fails closed to fixed. The envelope names budget_scale / budget_cents_effective / budget_cents_max only when the
+# key is written: a config without it writes the envelope it always wrote.
+#
+# Whole-run harness: adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash (main() sourced, invoke_dissenter stubbed, no model called).
+# Prices: one fixture alias at 100 USD per Mtok input and 0 output, so each voice costs tokens / 100 cents, with
+# tokens = diff bytes / 3 + 500 (the gate's own estimate) — 108,300 bytes → 366c, 62,700 → 214c, 208,500 → 700c.
+# =============================================================================
+
+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
+
+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bsc; }
+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
+
+_cfg() {  # <gate key> <budget_cents> [extra gate lines] — the gate under test, companion off, one priced primary
+    s3_config "hounfour:
+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-scale:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 100000000, output_per_mtok: 0}
+flatline_protocol:
+  $1:
+    enabled: true
+    model: fixture-scale
+    budget_cents: $2
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: false
+    fallback_chain: []
+${3:-}"
+}
+
+_diff_of() {  # <bytes> → $T/diff.patch of exactly that size (a header and one long line)
+    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( $1 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
+    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch" | tr -d ' ')" -eq "$1" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-1 the key absent: the shipped gate, byte for byte — estimate 366c over budget 200c is refused and the envelope names no scaling" {
+    _diff_of 108300
+    _cfg code_review 200
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "366" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
+    # exactly the keys the gate wrote before cycle-131
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | keys' <<<"$result")" = '["budget_cents","estimate_voices","estimated_cents","status","type"]' ]
+    grep -qF "Estimated cost (366c) exceeds budget (200c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    ! grep -q "budget_scale" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "an absent key was said"; return 1; }
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-2 budget_scale: fixed written explicitly keeps the configured budget (366c over 200c refused) and names the scaling, reason budget" {
+    _diff_of 108300
+    _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: fixed"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {status, reason, budget_scale, budget_cents, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max, estimated_cents}' <<<"$result")" \
+      = '{"status":"budget_exceeded","reason":"budget","budget_scale":"fixed","budget_cents":200,"budget_cents_effective":200,"budget_cents_max":600,"estimated_cents":366}' ]
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-3 budget_scale: diff — estimate 214c over budget 200c scales the budget to ceil(214 × 1.2) = 257c and the review runs, the envelope says so" {
+    _diff_of 62700
+    _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    grep -qx "fixture-scale" "$CALLS"
+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 214c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-scale 214c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "budget: budget_scale=diff — configured 200c, estimate 214c, effective 257c (max 600c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {budget_scale, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max}' <<<"$result")" = '{"budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents_effective":257,"budget_cents_max":600}' ]
+    [ "$(jq '.findings | length' <<<"$result")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-4 budget_scale: diff — estimate 700c caps the budget at budget_cents_max 600c and is refused (exit 4, budget_exceeded, reason budget)" {
+    _diff_of 208500
+    _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {status, reason, budget_scale, budget_cents, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max, estimated_cents}' <<<"$result")" \
+      = '{"status":"budget_exceeded","reason":"budget","budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents":200,"budget_cents_effective":600,"budget_cents_max":600,"estimated_cents":700}' ]
+    grep -qF "Estimated cost (700c) exceeds budget (600c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+    # a lower maximum is honoured: 214c with budget_cents_max 250 → ceil(256.8) = 257 is held to 250, and 214c fits under it
+    _diff_of 62700
+    _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: diff
+    budget_cents_max: 250"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "250" ]
+    # and a maximum below the estimate refuses: 214c with budget_cents_max 210
+    _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: diff
+    budget_cents_max: 210"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {reason, budget_cents_effective, budget_cents_max}' <<<"$result")" = '{"reason":"budget","budget_cents_effective":210,"budget_cents_max":210}' ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-5 a malformed budget_scale fails closed to fixed and is said: 366c over 200c is refused whatever the spelling (Diff, yes, a list, a map)" {
+    _diff_of 108300
+    local v
+    for v in "Diff" "yes" "[diff]" "{a: diff}" "1"; do
+        _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: $v"
+        result=$(s3_run review)
+        [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { echo "budget_scale: $v"; cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.budget_scale' <<<"$result")" = "fixed" ] || { echo "budget_scale: $v"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
+        grep -q "WARN: flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_scale=.* is not fixed or diff — fixed applies" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "budget_scale: $v not said"; return 1; }
+    done
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-6 a malformed budget_cents_max fails closed to fixed and is said (diff with a max of 6OO, -1, 600.5 or 060 keeps the configured budget)" {
+    _diff_of 62700
+    local v
+    for v in "6OO" "-1" "600.5" "060"; do
+        _cfg code_review 200 "    budget_scale: diff
+    budget_cents_max: $v"
+        result=$(s3_run review)
+        [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { echo "budget_cents_max: $v"; cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.budget_scale' <<<"$result")" = "fixed" ]
+        [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "200" ]
+        grep -qF "is not a whole number — budget_scale fixed applies" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "budget_cents_max: $v not said"; return 1; }
+    done
+}
+
+@test "BSC-7 the formula's other branches: a configured budget above ceil(estimate × 1.2) is kept, and one above the maximum is held to the maximum (min(max(…), max))" {
+    _diff_of 62700
+    _cfg code_review 300 "    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "300" ]
+    _cfg code_review 1000 "    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")" = "600" ]
+    # the helper itself: ceil in integer arithmetic, and fixed is the configured budget whatever the estimate
+    CONF_BUDGET_SCALE=diff CONF_BUDGET_CENTS_MAX=600
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 5)" = "6" ]       # ceil(6.0)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 10)" = "12" ]     # ceil(12.0)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 11)" = "14" ]     # ceil(13.2)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 214)" = "257" ]   # ceil(256.8)
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 150 0)" = "150" ]
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 0 700)" = "600" ]
+    CONF_BUDGET_SCALE=fixed
+    [ "$(_adv_budget_effective 200 700)" = "200" ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-8 each gate reads its own block: security_audit.budget_scale: diff scales the audit gate; the review gate without the key stays fixed" {
+    _diff_of 62700
+    s3_config "hounfour:
+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-scale:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 100000000, output_per_mtok: 0}
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: fixture-scale
+    budget_cents: 200
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: false
+    fallback_chain: []
+  security_audit:
+    enabled: true
+    model: fixture-scale
+    budget_cents: 200
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: false
+    fallback_chain: []
+    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run audit)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {type, budget_scale, budget_cents_effective}' <<<"$result")" = '{"type":"audit","budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents_effective":257}' ]
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | keys' <<<"$result")" = '["budget_cents","estimate_voices","estimated_cents","status","type"]' ]
+}
+
+@test "BSC-9 the shipped example config documents both keys under both gates with the default fixed and the formula, and the live config sets neither" {
+    local ex="$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml.example"
+    local gate
+    for gate in code_review security_audit; do
+        [ "$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${gate}.budget_scale" "$ex")" = "fixed" ] || { echo "$gate: budget_scale is not fixed in the example"; return 1; }
+        [ "$(yq eval ".flatline_protocol.${gate}.budget_cents_max" "$ex")" = "600" ] || { echo "$gate: budget_cents_max is not 600"; return 1; }
+    done
+    grep -qF "min(max(budget_cents, ceil(estimate × 1.2)), budget_cents_max)" "$ex"
+    if [[ -f "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml" ]]; then
+        [ "$(yq eval '.flatline_protocol.code_review.budget_scale // "absent"' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml")" = "absent" ]
+        [ "$(yq eval '.flatline_protocol.security_audit.budget_scale // "absent"' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.loa.config.yaml")" = "absent" ]
+    fi
+}
+
+@test "BSC-10 with the companion voice planned the scaling covers both voices' estimate and survives the fold: the folded two-voice envelope still names it" {
+    s3_config "hounfour:
+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-scale:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 100000000, output_per_mtok: 0}
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: fixture-scale
+    budget_cents: 0
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: true
+    fallback_chain: []
+    budget_scale: diff"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    grep -q "budget: estimate [0-9]*c over 2 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-scale [0-9]*c, companion claude-headless [0-9]*c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qx "fixture-scale" "$CALLS"
+    grep -qx "claude-headless" "$CALLS"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.companion_voice.planned' <<<"$result")" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '.metadata | {budget_scale, budget_cents_max}' <<<"$result")" = '{"budget_scale":"diff","budget_cents_max":600}' ]
+    # budget_cents 0 is the configured cap; diff lifted it to ceil(estimate × 1.2) — at least the estimate, never above 600
+    local est eff
+    est=$(sed -n 's/.*budget: estimate \([0-9]*\)c over 2 planned.*/\1/p' "$T/stderr.log" | head -1)
+    eff=$(jq '.metadata.budget_cents_effective' <<<"$result")
+    [ "$eff" = "$(( (est * 12 + 9) / 10 ))" ] || { echo "est=$est eff=$eff"; return 1; }
+}

+_na_finding() {  # <extra jq object> → one valid review finding on x.sh with a symbol anchor, plus the extra fields
+    jq -nc --argjson x "$1" '{id: "DISS-001", severity: "ADVISORY", category: "error-handling", anchor: "x.sh:do_thing",

python3 -I - "$manifest" "$review" "$executor" "$manifest_v1" "$head_dir" <<'PY'
import json, os, re, stat, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path, manifest_v1_path, head_dir = sys.argv[1:6]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
man_v1 = json.load(open(manifest_v1_path)) if manifest_v1_path else man
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

# ---- 1.3.0: head files, definition scopes, citation validity --------------------------
RANGE_CAP = 25      # a wider cited range credits only through its first line
SPAN_CAP = 400      # a longer definition falls back to ±FALLBACK around the site
FALLBACK = 20
BASH_HDR = (re.compile(r'^(\s*)(?:function\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\s*\(\)\s*\{?'),
            re.compile(r'^(\s*)function\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\s*\{'))
PY_HDR = re.compile(r'^(\s*)def\s+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\(')
BATS_HDR = re.compile(r'^()@test\s+"')
MD_HDR = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})(?:\s|$)')

import json, os, re, stat, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path, manifest_v1_path, head_dir = sys.argv[1:6]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
man_v1 = json.load(open(manifest_v1_path)) if manifest_v1_path else man
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:

    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):

        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited

    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

MD_HDR = re.compile(r'^(#{1,6})(?:\s|$)')

# Reviewer concerns — sprint-1 (PR: cycle-131 sprint-263, 35 files)

Phase 2 notes from the primary reviewer. The change under review is `pr/head.diff`; files under `pr/head/`.

## Suspected defects

1. `tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget-scale.bats` BSC-9 asserts the *live* `.loa.config.yaml` has no
   `budget_scale` key under either gate, while the same PR adds `budget_scale: fixed` to
   `.loa.config.yaml.example` (whose header says to copy sections into the live file). Any operator who
   copies the flatline section, or who enables `diff` (as this workspace's live config does), gets a red
   unit test. A test must not depend on an operator-owned, untracked file.
2. `evals/tests/ablation-grade.bats` AG-50 reads `evals/tests/fixtures/c131-oracle/<run>/{transcripts,task,dotclaude}`
   and pins exact results against "curated" `manifests/pr-17.json` and `manifests/v1/`. None of those
   fixtures or manifests are in the diff (35 files, no `evals/fixtures/review-prs/manifests/*`, no
   `evals/tests/fixtures/c131-oracle/*`). The PR title claims "curated multi-site labels, versioned re-grade".
3. `evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh` `close_line`: `CLOSE_ONE = \{.*\}\s*(?:#.*)?$` + `"{" in header`
   treats any function header whose trailing comment contains a `}` (e.g. `f() {  # writes ${OUT}`) as a
   one-line function, so its body gets no scope. Also the `}` indentation compare uses raw `len(t)-len(t.lstrip())`
   while header indentation used `expandtabs(8)` — tab-indented bash never finds its closing brace.
4. `evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh` `cmd_check` clause (d): "exactly the base commit over every ref" and
   "fsck --unreachable reports nothing" — any `git commit`/`git stash`/`git add; git reset` by the agent in the
   sandbox fails `oracle_closed` post-run → infrastructure_error → the arm is paused (a1_full in the suite).
   Only the "no later-only pinned blob / no remote / no alternates" parts are oracle-relevant.
5. `evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh` `repo_name_exempt`: the unit is the backtick span, so a bare
   `` `0xHoneyJar/loa` `` is exempt whenever the fixture holds the token anywhere; `gh api repos/`0xHoneyJar/loa`/…`
   would pass the contamination scan on pr-18.
6. `evals/harness/ablation-row.sh` `evkv` takes the LAST `key=` line; `took-effect.sh evidence_line`,
   `sandbox-mount.sh read_evidence` and `check_mount_closed` (`sed -n '1p'`) take the FIRST; `pipeline-run.sh`
   takes the last for copy_source. Inconsistent evidence reading.
7. `recall-vs-defects.sh valid_cite`: a range whose end is past EOF credits nothing even when its first line
   is valid (ordering of the two validity rules), while `file:N` alone credits.
8. `ablation-grade.sh oracle_scan`: `exposed_unknown` is only emitted when no range/must_match hit at all in a
   section; the header comment says "every other defect of that file".
9. `.loa.config.yaml.example` now writes `budget_scale: fixed` explicitly, so copying it flips
   `CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET` and changes the envelope shape (adds reason/budget_* keys) despite "absent key is
   the shipped gate byte for byte".
10. No CHANGELOG entry in the diff; `PR.md` is a one-line title (no AC walkthrough).

## Areas I'd like a second opinion on

- `_sm_oracle_py diff_paths` hunk-count tracking and `header_names` on unusual `diff --git` headers.
- `oracle_plan` / `split_segments` / `classify` edge cases (false positives via `.` or `..` tokens, `cd -`).
- `ablation-report.py` partition keys (`"2 · pin … · rule …"`) flowing into `version_order` callers.
- jq validation block in `ablation-row.sh` (`positions_rule`, `need` on 1.4 fields).
- `_normalize_finding_for_validation` jq concatenation and the schema-enforced numeric-anchor branch.

--- findings:
DISS-001 [BLOCKING] (gpt-5.5-pro) anchor=evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:close_line line=308 status=valid
  desc: Multiline Python signatures incorrectly terminate the function scope. For a conventional signature such as `def f(\n    argument,\n):`, the closing `):` has the definition's indentation, so this condition returns before the function body.
  fail: Every body line receives no function scope. A citation and planted defect in the same function, but more than three lines apart, are consequently graded as a miss, producing incorrect recall scores and potentially failing an otherwise passing evaluation.
  fix: Identify the end of the complete Python signature before checking body dedentation, preferably using Python tokenization or AST function spans.

DISS-C-001 [ADVISORY] (claude-headless) anchor=.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:_adv_conf_budget_scale line=163 status=valid
  desc: When `yq eval ... | tag` fails (no .loa.config.yaml present, unparsable YAML, yq missing), the fallback echoes the literal `unreadable`, which is neither `!!null` nor empty. The function then sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET=true, logs a WARN with the odd text `budget_scale='(a unreadable, not a string)' is not fixed or diff`, and the envelope gains budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max and `reason: budget`. Every other config read in load_adversarial_config degrades silently to its default on a yq failure; this one changes the envelope shape, contradicting the documented contract that an absent key leaves the envelope byte-for-byte unchanged.
  fail: Runs in a checkout with no .loa.config.yaml (or a temporarily unreadable one) emit a spurious WARN on every invocation and produce a different envelope shape than the same config did before this change, which can break consumers or fixtures that compare the metadata object exactly.
  fix: Treat a yq failure as absent: `_bt=$(yq ... 2>/dev/null || echo '!!null')`, or test `[[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]]` before reading and return 0 otherwise, so CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET stays false unless a key is genuinely written.

DISS-C-002 [ADVISORY] (claude-headless) anchor=.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:main line=4750 status=valid
  desc: `[[ "$_budget_meta" == "{}" ]] || result=$(echo "$result" | jq --argjson bm "$_budget_meta" ...)` assumes `_budget_meta` was initialised at the budget gate ~300 lines earlier. If any path reaches the envelope assembly without passing through the gate (the variable is `local` and only assigned there), `$_budget_meta` is empty, the test is false, `jq --argjson bm ""` fails, and under `set -e` the failed assignment either aborts main or clobbers `result` with an empty string after all voices have already been paid for.
  fail: A control-flow path that skips the pre-dispatch estimate (e.g. a future flag or an early branch) turns a completed dissent run into an aborted one with an empty envelope.
  fix: Default the guard: `[[ "${_budget_meta:-\{\}}" == "{}" ]] || ...`, or initialise `local _budget_meta="{}"` at the top of main alongside the other locals.

DISS-C-003 [ADVISORY] (claude-headless) anchor=evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:close_line line=287 status=valid
  desc: Two end-of-definition heuristics misfire on bash. None are among the 35 files, so the "curated multi-site labels, versioned re-grade" in the title has nothing behind it.
- **Grader scope bug on wrapped Python signatures.** The end-of-definition rule returns at the first line indented no deeper than the `def`, so `def f(\n    arg,\n):` closes on the argument line and the function body never gets a scope. I reproduced it. The gpt-5.5-pro dissent voice flagged the same line as BLOCKING.

Seven medium observations include: the one-line-function regex misfiring on headers whose comment contains `}`; the standalone grader falling back to the agent-writable `pr/head` for scope and validity; closed-mount clause (d) failing `oracle_closed` and pausing the control arm on any agent `git commit` or `stash`; the backtick-span exemption letting a bare `` `0xHoneyJar/loa` `` through the contamination scan; a failed `yq` read flipping the envelope shape; two functions of 190 and 120 lines; and no CHANGELOG or AC walkthrough. Eight low observations cover tab indentation, first-versus-last evidence reads, rule ordering, and schema drift.

Next step for the engineer is to address the three blocking items and re-request `/review-sprint sprint-1`.
